blocks.text: Judges as a whole moves from incomplete possession and covenant indictment through repeated deliverances toward internal idolatry, atrocity, and civil war. Within that movement, Gideon’s story and the following account of Abimelech can be read as a turning point: deliverance becomes entangled with dynastic ambition, idolatry, and violence within Israel. This frames the troubling developments in Judges 8—including the proposed hereditary rule, Gideon’s ephod, and conflict among Israelites—as part of the book’s worsening disorder, though the precise interpretation of this turning point remains disputed.
